properties.name: The instructions can be read in parts, and the signpost speaks to the agent
properties.rationale:
Both items are from Alex's 2026-08-27 field report, re-measured against 0.41.0 source before anything was designed.

⭐ THE MEASUREMENT CORRECTED THE RECORDED DIAGNOSIS, which is why it was taken first. `fact:defect-the-served-instructions-put-their-standing-rules-where-a-client-cap-deletes-them` (2026-08-15) said the ordering is "worst-first-lost" and that report-friction sits AFTER the cut, making the defect self-sealing — the agent loses the instruction telling it to report the loss. Measured on the current document, that is no longer true: the standing rules sit at 3.5%, 4.5% and 7.6%, and "## If reflow2 gets in your way, say so" sits at 63%, INSIDE his 73% cut. It reached him. What he actually lost was the tail — the gap→question handshake at 73.8% and the entire tool inventory at 78%. That fact proposed three fix shapes; the first was already done, and this builds the other two.

⚠️ THE OBVIOUS FIX WAS THE WRONG ONE, and measuring stopped it. `get_instructions` sends 56,257 bytes for a 26,846-byte document — 2.1×, the exact duplication removed from every other tool in August for being "the difference between an answer a client could read and one it refused". The tempting move is to remove it here too. THAT WOULD HAVE MADE THINGS WORSE FOR THE ONE USER WHO REPORTED IT: the prose tools reach him precisely BECAUSE they duplicate into `content`, and stripping the copy would have left him with nothing at all. Sectioning solves the size without taking away the field he can actually read.

📌 THE SIGNPOST CHANGE IS OPTION (d) OF `dec:idea-how-does-a-content-only-client-get-an-answer`, taken deliberately as COMPLEMENTARY. That node records (d) as strictly improving every other option and foreclosing none, so this does not pre-empt Alex's pending answer on which protocol revision his client negotiated — the question that still decides between (a), (b) and (c). The defect it fixes is that the stub instructed a party not in the room: the AGENT reads it and cannot change its own harness, so for exactly the population it was written for it named no action anybody could take.
properties.subject: system
properties.summary:
`get_instructions` gains an optional `section`, and every reply now carries a `sections` manifest with `total_bytes` and `returned_bytes` — so a client-side cap is DETECTABLE (one field disagrees with what the reader holds) and RECOVERABLE (the parts can be fetched one at a time). The largest section is 11,260 bytes against the ~19.5 KB cap that truncated a real consumer twice, so every section is individually deliverable on the harness that could not take the whole document. An unknown slug is refused and lists the legal ones. A test pins that the sections rejoin into the document byte for byte, and everything before the first `##` becomes `overview` so no byte is unreachable by slug.

Separately, the `STRUCTURED_ONLY` signpost was rewritten to address the AGENT rather than the client: it now names the prose tools, the fact that refusals arrive in `content` intact, and `export_graph` with a `path` — and states that these do not replace `search_design` before a create or `loop_status` before finishing.
